turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My mum has a shoebox of old prints from the seventies. What's the best way to scan them?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For a shoebox, a flatbed scanner gives the best quality, but a phone scanning app is much faster. How many are we talking?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Maybe four hundred? Some are stuck together.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Don't pull stuck ones apart dry, they can tear. A photo conservator can separate them, or just scan the others first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. And the app, is that really good enough?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: For sharing with family, yes. The good apps remove glare by taking a few shots at different angles. If you want to print them big later, use a scanner at six hundred dpi.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She'd love to see them on the telly at Christmas.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then the app is plenty. Write the year and names in the file name as you go, while your mum is there to remember who's who.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, she'll love that. She'll tell a story for every single one.
